Position 1: N-Me (`n1C`)

Wait, the reaction type is "C-C bond formation".
Typical C-C bond formation for pyrazolones involves the condensation of a ketone (or beta-dicarbonyl compound) with a hydrazine derivative.
Here, the pyrazolone ring is formed from:

Actually, a common precursor for 1-methyl-3-phenyl-5-methylpyrazol-4-one is ethyl 2-oxobutanoate (or ethyl acetoacetate) + N-methyl-N-phenylhydrazine? No, the N-phenyl and N-methyl are on the hydrazine.

So the carbonyl component must be a beta-keto acid/ester with that amide group.
